requirement_text.ISS-0216: Letflow.Api.Pagination.decode_cursor/4 trusts its caller-supplied prefix with no non-empty guard, a real bypass path once REQ-072-onward endpoints call it. check_prefix/2 (lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex) uses a size guard (byte_size(decoded) >= byte_size(prefix) and String.starts_with?(decoded, prefix)) that trivially passes if prefix is an empty string, since every decoded cursor starts with the empty string -- an empty prefix defeats the cross-endpoint isolation this parameter exists to provide. Filed 2026-08-21 as unreachable-but-real-risk (REQ-072 routing layer was pending); NOW LIVE -- confirmed 2026-08-26 that real route handlers (lib/letflow/routers/audit.ex, tasks.ex, instances.ex, routers/tenants.ex, routers/identity.ex, definitions.ex) already call decode_cursor/4 with hardcoded non-empty module-attribute prefixes. The guard itself is still missing.

result.summary:
Checked lib/letflow/design/iss0216-pagination-prefix-guard.md against step-01's diagnosis (handoffs/WF03-ISS0216-20260826/step-01-issue-fixer.json) and step-02's six acceptance criteria.

PASS on five of six checks:
1. Exact clause named: check_prefix/2 in lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex gains a new leading function-head clause matching prefix == ""; decode_cursor/4's with-chain and @spec are stated unchanged. Correctly identifies the same root cause step-01 traced to lines 211-218.
2. Error-shape decision is explicit, not deferred: raise ArgumentError, with a three-part rationale (why not reuse :wrong_endpoint, why not a new {:error, :invalid_prefix} tuple, why raising is INV-8-compliant since INV-8's own moduledoc text scopes 'no unhandled crashes' to network-facing input and prefix is caller-internal per step-01's 9-site audit). This is a reasoned choice, not a TBD, and is flagged in §5 as overridable with a stated one-line alternative -- that is disclosure, not deferral.
3. @spec deltas stated for both functions: check_prefix/2's @spec (:ok | {:error, :wrong_endpoint}) is stated unchanged; decode_cursor/4's @spec is stated unchanged (raise is not part of an Elixir @spec return type). Both explicit.
4. TEST-DESIGNER scope named in §4: mandatory empty-prefix case (assert_raise ArgumentError, mirroring step-01's live reproduction), non-regression on all five existing return-value cases, an optional boundary-prefix case, and an explicit 'test only through public decode_cursor/4' constraint.
6. Handoff mechanics: step-02's own handoff correctly names next_action 'Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR'.

FAIL on check 5 (no implementation code in the design doc). §2.1 does not merely name or describe the new clause -- it gives a complete, literal, copy-paste-ready Elixir function clause with a full body:

  defp check_prefix(_decoded, ""), do:
    raise ArgumentError, "Letflow.Api.Pagination.decode_cursor/4 called with an empty prefix -- prefix must be a non-empty, hardcoded per-endpoint literal (see moduledoc INV-1/INV-5); an empty prefix defeats cross-endpoint cursor isolation (ISS-0216)"

  defp check_prefix(decoded, prefix) do
    # existing body, unchanged
  end

This is a real .ex function clause -- a defp head, a full do: body, and a literal, finished error-message string -- not a signature or type shape. It is exactly the kind of implementation-ready code CODE-DESIGNER's own role charter and WF-02 Step 1b (and by extension this WF-03 fix-design step) forbid: 'no real .ex/.exs bodies -- signatures and type shapes only.' Quoting the *existing* check_prefix/2 body in §0 for diagnosis context is fine (it is existing shipped code being cited, not new code being authored); §2.1's new clause is different in kind -- it is new code CODE-DESIGNER wrote that ELIXIR-DEV could paste verbatim into pagination.ex with zero authorship left to do. Per WF-02 Step 1b / this workflow's FAIL rule ('FAIL immediately and completely on any single failed check -- no partial credit'), this one violation fails the whole design regardless of the other five checks passing.

No other gaps found: no TBD/deferral language anywhere else in the document, cross-module dependencies correctly stated as none (owned_modules is exactly lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex, no route-handler change), and the design's reasoning was checked line-by-line against step-01's call-site audit (all 9 sites, hardcoded-literal origin) and reproduction output -- it does not contradict or overstate anything step-01 established.
